10.1002_adma.75534: Aqueous Zn–I 2 batteries are promising for sustainable energy storage systems, yet their practical performance is severely limited by the formation and shuttling of polyiodide intermediates. Here, we report a site separation strategy to block the generation paths of polyiodides and address the related issues from the source. This is realized with a site‐separated polymer (SSP) binder that strongly and selectively confines I 2 and I − at varied functional groups on different side chains. It disrupts their coupling to generate polyiodides chemically. Meanwhile, these effective interactions regulate the thermodynamic features of iodine species, which disfavors the formation of polyiodide intermediates and promotes direct I 2 /I − conversion during electrochemical reactions. The binder also reinforces cathode integrity at different iodine loadings. Therefore, the I 2 /SSP cathode delivers 212 mAh g −1 capacity at 0.2 A g −1 and retains 102 mAh g −1 at 50 A g −1 , superior to 172 mAh g −1 /11 mAh g −1 with the conventional polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) binder. I 2 /SSP also realizes 97.1% capacity retention over 31000 cycles at 20 A g −1 , again far exceeding 46.8% after 20000 cycles for I 2 /PVDF. Under a high iodine loading of 50 mg cm −2 , the I 2 /SSP cathode further achieves 10.1 mAh cm −2 capacity with 97.9% retention over 400 cycles.
10.1002_aenm.202504054: Polymer‐based electrolytes have emerged as attractive candidates for solid‐state batteries owing to their facile processability, excellent interfacial compatibility, and cost‐effectiveness. However, their excessive crystallinity, disrupted ion pathways, and inadequate mechanical performance directly impair ionic conductivity and cycling stability. Herein, a synergistic strategy is reported to simultaneously incorporate LiCl and ZrCl 4 in a poly (ethylene oxide)/poly (vinylidene fluoride) (PEO/PVDF) electrolyte matrix to achieve enhanced structural and electrochemical properties. The introduction of LiCl and Lewis‐acidic ZrCl 4 increased the lithium‐ion transference number to 0.56 and promoted the formation of a stable, LiF‐ and LiCl‐rich electrolyte interphase layer on the lithium anode. The symmetric cells exhibited a critical current density of 3.1 mA cm −2 and demonstrated stable cycling for over 400 h at a current density of 0.7 mA cm −2 , and full cells paired with LiFePO 4 cathode (3.8 mg cm −2 ) retained 88.4% of their initial capacity after 1000 cycles. The electrolyte exhibits a tensile strength of 12 MPa with an elongation of 210%, achieving an excellent balance between mechanical strength, flexibility, and processability. This dual‐filler strategy provides a practical and effective approach for enhancing polymer electrolyte performance and holds great promise for broad applications in solid‐state lithium batteries.
10.1016_j.est.2026.123190: Electrochromic energy storage devices (EcESDs) still meet many challenges, demanding continuous materials development and device engineering for practical applications. Herein, we introduce two conjugated 3,4-propylenedioxythiophene (ProDOT)-based polymers directly deposited by electropolimerization on rigid/flexible substrates (ITO-coated glass/PET) as electrodes for EcESDs. The starting monomers were functionalized with two different polar groups, short hydroxymethyl and long oligooxyethylene-benzoester fragment, to boost the ionic conductivity and enhance the coating adhesion to the working electrode surface for improved charge transfer. Among electropolymerized polymers, the one substituted with a long polar chain exhibited outstanding capacitive and electrochromic performance in a three-electrode configuration, e.g. capacitance of 9.96 mF/cm 2 at 0.01 mA/cm 2 , high optical contrast of 83%, color switching in sub-second time frames, and remarkable coloration efficiency, of 1036 cm 2 /C, outperforming many conjugated polymers reported to date. The EcESDs assembled on both rigid and flexible electrodes without the use of any additional storage layer also confirmed a better electrochromic response from this polymer, affording optical contrast of 54.86% and coloration efficiency of 824 cm 2 /C. Unexpectedly, both electropolymerized polymers displayed similar energy storage performance (1.04 mF/cm 2 at 0.01 mA), as a consequence of a more ideal device state attained by the hydroxymethyl-functionalized polymer in terms of electrical contacts, internal series resistance, balanced charge between the electrodes, and others. Notably, the flexible devices also showed capacitive performances comparable to those of the rigid counterparts, even in a bent state, placing the investigated polymers among promising candidates for the next-generation bendable and smart energy storage devices.
10.1016_j.ultsonch.2026.108012: This study systematically compared ultrasound-assisted electrolyzed water extraction (UAEWE), ultrasound-assisted extraction (UAE), traditional acid extraction (AE), and commercially available hawthorn pectin (CHP) in terms of pectin yield, physicochemical properties, structural characteristics, and antioxidant activity. The objective was to evaluate the feasibility of UAEWE as a sustainable alternative for hawthorn pectin production and explore its potential applications. Results indicated that UAEWE-extracted pectin achieved the highest yield (7.21 ± 0.13%) and galacturonic acid (GalA) content (87.35 ± 0.37 g/100 g), significantly surpassing UAE (5.96 ± 0.06%; 82.28 ± 0.49 g/100 g) and AE (4.53 ± 0.15%; 76.08 ± 0.96 g/100 g). However, UAEWE-extracted pectin exhibited lower esterification degree (63.13 ± 0.08%), weight-average molecular weight (223.92 ± 4.22 kDa), and particle size (3.56 ± 0.45 μm) than the other samples. Monosaccharide composition analysis revealed similar sugar profiles among all samples, although relative proportions differed. Microstructural characterization showed that UAEWE-extracted pectin possessed a highly porous architecture, consistent with its superior extraction yield. FTIR and NMR analyses confirmed no significant structural alterations among the pectin samples. Rheological measurements demonstrated that UAEWE-extracted pectin exhibited the lowest apparent viscosity at 1% concentration, pH 3, and low shear rates. Moreover, UAEWE-derived pectin showed enhanced antioxidant activity compared with UAE, AE, and CHP samples. These findings highlight UAEWE as a promising extraction strategy for hawthorn pectin, offering reduced acid usage, cost-effectiveness, and environmental sustainability. The resulting pectin, characterized by high GalA content and antioxidant capacity, shows potential for bioactive compound encapsulation and functional food applications.
10.1021_acsami.6c11799: Aqueous zinc metal batteries (AZMBs) are constrained by water-induced side reactions and non-uniform Zn deposition. Herein, we introduce 3,4-dihydroxycyclobut-3-ene-1,2-dione (SA) as an electrolyte additive to regulate molecular interface chemistry. The introduction of SA disrupts the intrinsic hydrogen-bond network in the electrolyte, suppressing the activity of free water. Density functional theory calculations further demonstrate that SA preferentially binds to the Zn (100) and (101) surfaces over the (002) plane, which effectively limits the growth of high-energy facets and promotes oriented nucleation along the (002) texture, yielding a dense and uniform zinc deposit. Benefiting from these synergistic effects, the Zn//Zn symmetric cell achieves a stable cycling lifespan exceeding 2500 h, while the Zn//Cu asymmetric cell maintains a high Coulombic efficiency of 99.4% over 1000 cycles. This work offers an effective pathway for enhancing the performance of AZMBs.
10.1021_acssuschemeng.6c04808: Dielectric ceramic capacitors with superior energy storage performance serve as core components for next-generation advanced pulsed power systems and miniaturized electronic devices. However, the performance optimization of bulk dielectric ceramics is constrained by the inherent difficulty of simultaneously achieving high polarization and high efficiency. To address this issue, we propose a high-entropy strategy to construct the superparaelectric critical state—a crossover region from superparaelectric to relaxor state—for tuning the polarization configuration. Through rational compositional design, we incorporate Sr0.7Sm0.2(Zr0.5Ta0.4)O3 linear dielectric into a tetragonal Bi0.375Na0.375Ba0.25TiO3 matrix with high dielectric permittivity and large polarization, successfully shifting the maximum dielectric constant to near room temperature, enhancing rapid domain switching, and reducing hysteresis. Multiscale structural characterization reveals that the high-entropy design introduces strong local disorder to construct dynamic polar nanodomains, enabling the concurrent achievement of both high polarization and high efficiency. Consequently, the optimized ceramic delivers superior energy storage performance, including a recoverable energy density of 8.52 J/cm3 with an ultrahigh 93.86% efficiency and decent thermal stability (25–150 °C). This work provides a viable paradigm for designing high-performance dielectric ceramics for advanced capacitive energy storage applications.
